appearance_facts.fact: Title: 'Monthly Sales for Store B in City Y' is in bold, black text, positioned at the top-left of the chart area.
Vertical axis is labeled 'Sales', with numerical ticks from 0 to 600, increasing upward.
Horizontal axis is labeled 'Month', with tick marks for 'April', 'May', and 'June' from left to right.
A horizontal dashed line labeled 'Average' is drawn at the 550 level, spanning across the chart above the bars.
The bar for April is the tallest, extending to a height just below the 550 line, visually above the average.
The bar for May is the shortest, ending at approximately the 325 level, visually below the average.
The bar for June is the second tallest, ending at approximately the 475 level, visually below the average.
The April bar is taller than the June bar, which is taller than the May bar.

printed_facts.fact: Chart title: 'Monthly Sales for Store B in City Y'.
Y-axis label: 'Sales', with scale from 0 to 600.
Horizontal dashed line labeled 'Average' at the 550 level.
Bar for April reaches a value just below 550.
Bar for May reaches a value of approximately 325.
Bar for June reaches a value of approximately 475.
The form requires selecting 'June' for 'Review month' and 'Monthly bonus status routing' for 'Operations program'.

public_definitions: The 'June sales route' option must be chosen based on the comparison of June's sales to the average line on the chart.
The 'above-average sales bonus response' option corresponds to June sales being above the 550 average line.
The 'low-sales response' option corresponds to June sales being below the 550 average line.
The 'normal sales monitoring' option corresponds to June sales being at or near the 550 average line.
uncertain: The exact numerical value of the June bar is not labeled, so the comparison is approximate.
